timeline.basis: No fixed day-based statutory timeline was stated; processing time depends on the feasibility check, estimate preparation, and when the applicant pays the estimate/consolidated fee.
timeline.text: The application is tracked at every stage on the Nivesh Mitra dashboard; overall duration depends on UPPCL's feasibility check and estimate preparation and on how quickly the applicant pays the estimate fee, rather than a fixed day count.

deemedApproval.text: No deemed-approval mechanism currently applies; the expert recommended that complete deemed approval would not be appropriate for the final connection (given public safety/network security) but suggested it could be considered for intermediate administrative stages such as document scrutiny or file movement, subject to conditions.

validity.text: No validity period once the connection is released; it continues subject to timely bill payment, maintaining the sanctioned load, and compliance with applicable safety regulations.

fees.text: Processing fee paid online at the time of application, based on electricity load, ranging from INR 25 to INR 50,000. Processing fee for line shifting ranges from INR 1,000 to INR 25,000, and the security deposit ranges from INR 100 to INR 5,000.

findings.text: The process is fully online, end-to-end, on the Nivesh Mitra single window portal for commercial, industrial and institutional users; no offline steps were flagged by the expert.
No fixed day-based timeline is given for the overall connection process; duration depends on the feasibility check, estimate preparation, and when the applicant pays the estimate fee.
Processing fee is based on electricity load and ranges from INR 25 to INR 50,000; line-shifting processing fee ranges from INR 1,000 to INR 25,000; security deposit ranges from INR 100 to INR 5,000.

Expert suggested deemed approval could be considered for intermediate administrative stages (e.g., document scrutiny, file movement) while keeping final energization subject to technical verification and safety compliance.
Connections above a load threshold are routed through a separate portal (Jhatpat) rather than Nivesh Mitra.
Major challenges arise from incomplete applications and submission of incorrect or insufficient documents.
Delays occur in fulfilling technical requirements such as infrastructure augmentation in certain locations.
Higher connected loads require detailed technical examination to ensure network reliability and safety, as distinct from standard low-load connections.
Expert recommended improved applicant awareness and standardized document checklists to reduce incomplete submissions.
Recommended complete digital processing and better integration of departmental systems to cut down repeat queries.
Recommended online scheduling of inspections/feasibility visits.
Recommended greater automation of internal workflows and strengthened GIS-based planning and digital monitoring.

Risk-based classification was recommended: standard commercial and low-load industrial connections processed through simplified procedures, while high-load consumers continue to undergo detailed technical examination.
Uttar Pradesh has already implemented many digital-service-delivery reforms seen in other leading states (end-to-end online processing, real-time tracking, automated workflow management).
There is scope to reduce duplication in document submission and further digitize compliance reporting wherever feasible.

Post-approval, consumers must maintain installations per safety standards, pay bills on time, maintain the sanctioned load, obtain approval before increasing load, permit inspections, and comply with the Electricity Act, Supply Code, and safety regulations.
Recommended expanding GIS-based network planning and predictive load assessment to strengthen service delivery.

gaps.text: No specific day-based processing timeline is given for the electricity connection process, unlike the other UP licenses (FAL, FNO, RSE), which each cite explicit statutory day figures.

Deemed approval status for this service is not an existing legal provision per the discussion — only a recommendation by the expert for intermediate stages; the current status is effectively 'no deemed approval.'
No specific day counts given for how long the feasibility check (Step 7) or estimate preparation (Step 7-8) typically take.
Fully digital, end-to-end Nivesh Mitra process already in place for new electricity connections, cited by the expert as a best practice relative to other states.

Multiple reforms recommended but not yet implemented: risk-based simplified processing for standard/low-load connections, GIS-based planning, deemed approval at intermediate stages, and AI-enabled scrutiny.
The specific load threshold above which applications are routed to the separate Jhatpat portal instead of Nivesh Mitra is not specified.

licenses.issuingAuthority: Chief Inspector of Factories / Labour Commissioner Organisation (UP Labour Department) approves and issues the license; Government of Uttar Pradesh

timeline.basis: Factories Act, 1948 (Section 2(cb)) / Manufacture, Storage and Import of Hazardous Chemical Rules, 1989 (Rule 2(ja)) — statutory period for plan disposal by the Chief Inspector.
timeline.text: The plan of a factory must be disposed of within 15 working days of online receipt by the Chief Inspector's office; this extends to 30 working days for factories carrying out hazardous processes. Where defects/deviations are found at inspection, the applicant is typically given 15 days to rectify and upload a compliance report.

documents: Structural stability certificate from an approved architect/engineer
Sale deed or rent agreement of premises

deemedApproval.text: Plans not rejected within 15 working days (30 for hazardous-process factories) are deemed approved, and the licence is also deemed approved; the site plan approval letter and licence are then issued by the Chief Inspector immediately, with the applicant informed by e-mail and registered mobile number.

validity.text: Valid for up to 10 years at a time, depending on the category of the factory, as provided under the U.P. Factories Rules, 1950.

fees.text: Statutory fee is based entirely on number of employees, payable online (Internet Banking, RajKosh, or other online modes). The document gives two different figures for this fee: the process-flow (Step 6) states INR 150 to 35,000, while the separate Statutory Fee section states INR 100 to 7,000 — see gaps.

licenses.issuingAuthority: Fire Department (UP Police – Fire Service Headquarters), Government of Uttar Pradesh — competent authority approves the Fire NOC

timeline.basis: Statutory timelines under the Uttar Pradesh Fire Services process.
timeline.text: Provisional NOC (prior to construction), Completion/Final NOC (post-construction/installation), and Renewal of Fire NOC are each to be processed within 15 working days.

deemedApproval.text: The expert confirmed deemed approval is not possible for Fire NOC: if the concerned official does not respond within the stipulated 15 working days, action is instead taken against the responsible officer for the delay, rather than the NOC being deemed granted.

validity.text: Under Rule 43 (unless sooner cancelled): 5 years for residential buildings (other than hotels); 3 years for non-residential buildings except hotels, hospitals, assembly buildings, hazardous storage and high-hazard industrial occupancies; 1 year for hotels, hospitals, assembly buildings, hazardous storage and high-hazard industrial occupancies. The State Government may, by order and after recording reasons, reduce or increase this period.

fees.text: The Statutory Fee section states there is no processing fee for Fire NOC; however, Step 6 of the process flow states the applicant pays a prescribed processing fee online — these two statements are inconsistent within the same document (see gaps).

timeline.basis: Section 4-B(1), Uttar Pradesh Shops and Commercial Establishments Act, 1962 — deemed registration if the Registering Officer takes no action within 30 days; same-day grant possible if documents are complete and correct.
timeline.text: The stated application timeline is 30 days. Under Section 4-B(1), if a complete application receives no approval, rejection or objection within 30 days it is deemed registered; if all documents are complete and correct, registration may also be granted the same day.

documents: Photograph of the shop front prominently showing the name board

deemedApproval.text: Section 4-B(1) of the Uttar Pradesh Shops and Commercial Establishments Act, 1962 provides for deemed registration: if a complete application is not approved, rejected, or objected to within 30 days, registration is deemed granted. If all documents are complete and correct, registration may also be granted the same day.

validity.text: The registration certificate is valid for the lifetime of the shop/commercial establishment or until it ceases to exist; no renewal is required.

fees.text: A one-time registration fee based on the category of the shop/establishment and, in certain categories, the number of employees, ranging from INR 2,250 to INR 75,000.
